lawyer:
Mr. M.A. Mannan, Advocate, with Mr. Mansur Habib, Advocate ----- for the petitioners. 
Mr. Sultan Ahmed, Deputy Attorney-General ----- for the State.
parties:
Abdul Majid & Ors.
Vs.
The State
full_judgment: 9. Mr. Sultan Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the state has referred to us the portion of the statement made in the First Information Report wherein the informant has mentioned the names of the accused petitioners as the persons who are said to have held out threats to the victim some time previous to the date of murder of Rumi on 7.5.86 stating that they would kill him. It is submitted that in the First Information Report there are certain indications which give rise to presumption about the involvement of the accused petitioners and three others in abetting the commission of the offence by giving order and hence it can not be said that there is no material in the case against the accused petitioners. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that the submission of the charge sheet by the police after investigation also speaks of the existence of prima facie case against the accused petitioners. Under such circumstances, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that quashing of criminal proceeding is not called for as it will amount to interference with the normal course of criminal justice. The defence plea, if there be any, could be tested at the time or trial but not at this stage in an interlocutory proceeding, the learned Deputy-Attorney General further submits. The learned Advocate for the accused petitioners again rieterates that there being nothing incriminatory against the accused petitioners in the First Information Report, in the confessional statements of other six accused persons, the submission of the charge sheet is an embellishment and if the proceedings is allowed to continue it would defeat the end of justice, or in other words occasion the abuse of the process of the court and, therefore, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners emphataticully submits that interference by this court at this stage is called for to secure the ends of justice. In support of his contention the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners have referred to a number of decisions of the Appellate Division and High court Division of our Supreme Court. The principle of law relating to quashing of criminal proceeding having been clearly settled in the series of decisions of our court, we are not to travel beyond those for getting guide line for a decision in the instant case. The decisions cited before us are 28 DLR(AD) 38, 24 DLR (Dhaka) 448, 32 DLR (Dhaka) 182, 32 DLR (AD) 1, 34 DLR (H.C) 377, 36 DLR (AD) 14, 38 DLR (AD) 18, PLD 1976 Peshwar 255, BLD 1988 (AD) 93, BLD 1988-65 and 71 and 1 BCR (AD) 68.
